summary.en: Lebanese police arrested two Hezbollah suspects caught moving explosives near the Lebanon‑Syria border, while an Israeli drone strike wounded six people in Lebanon close to the Syrian frontier. The Israeli Defense Forces then carried out airstrikes that killed a Syrian operative accused of planning attacks on Israel from the Lebanon‑Syria border area. These actions target Hezbollah logistics and Iranian‑backed Syrian actors operating along the frontier, a shift from earlier artillery exchanges and larger bombardments. The UCDP recorded 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Libanesisk politi arresterte to Hezbollah-mistenkte som ble tatt på fersk gjerning med å flytte sprengstoff nær Libanon‑Syria‑grensen, mens et israelsk dronerammet seks personer i Libanon nær den syriske grensen. Det israelske forsvaret gjennomførte deretter luftangrep som drepte en syrisk operativ anklaget for å planlegge angrep på Israel fra Libanon‑Syria‑grenseområdet. Disse handlingene retter seg mot Hezbollas logistikk og iransk‑støttede syriske aktører som opererer langs grensen, en endring fra tidligere artilleribytte og større bombardementer. UCDP registrerte 4 335 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
